ev.q: A rabies-infected tamandua was translocated from Virginia to Tennessee, exposing multiple persons.
Risk assessments for 22 persons were completed to determine the need for rabies postexposure prophylaxis (rPEP); rPEP was recommended for 13 persons
rPEP was recommended for 13 persons, all of whom agreed to receive it.
Seven persons received this recommendation either because of known or presumed exposure to saliva

public_health_question.v: How did a rabid tamandua translocated from Virginia to Tennessee become infected, and which exposed persons needed rabies postexposure prophylaxis?

ev.q: TDH conducted an investigation to confirm the rabies result, characterize the rabies variant, and ascertain an exposure risk assessment
Translocation of an Anteater ( Tamandua tetradactyla ) Infected with Rabies from Virginia to Tennessee Resulting in Multiple Human Exposures, 2021
All 22 persons identified with potential exposure completed the risk assessment.
TDH developed an assessment tool to identify persons potentially exposed to the tamandua during the rabies viral shedding period
All 22 persons identified with potential exposure completed the risk assessment.
molecular characterization determined that the rabies virus was most similar to the rabies virus variant (RVV) observed in raccoons
a South American collared anteater ( Tamandua tetradactyla ) in Washington County, Tennessee.
Postexposure vaccination was received by 13 persons. No human cases occurred.

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension appears; exposed persons are defined by occupation as a route of exposure, which is not SES.

notes: Single animal case with a contact risk assessment; counts of exposed persons and rPEP recommendations are descriptive only. Phylogenetic analysis is a case-characterization step, not a procedure.
